1	# Autotuner → Product-Build Linkage (operator runbook)
2	
3	**What this covers.** How to make `compile.py`'s autotuned launch parameters
4	ACTIVE in the shipped `grokking_optimizers/_ops*.so` — produce winners, rebuild
5	so the per-TU flags are baked in, verify they actually landed, and re-run the
6	parity + roofline gates against the tuned binary.
7	
8	**Background — lever (b).** The `compile.py` JIT autotuner builds and times
9	kernel variants and picks a winner per `(optimizer, model, arch)`. Historically
10	that winner only reached a header that nothing on the install path included, so
11	the product `.so` shipped the in-header defaults — the autotuner was
12	decorative. The linkage now is:
13	
14	```
15	compile.py build_jit  --(write-on-win, atomic)-->  grokking_optimizers/_kernel_tuned.json
16	                                                          |
17	pip install -e .  /  ./build.sh                           v
18	   setup.py TunedBuildExtension  --reads JSON, injects per-TU nvcc flags-->  _ops*.so
19	```
20	
21	The five SAFE per-TU dims are applied: `-DSG_TUNED_BLOCK_SIZE`,
22	`-DSG_TUNED_VEC_WIDTH`, `-DSG_TUNED_UNROLL`, `-DSG_TUNED_ASYNC_DEPTH`, and
23	`--maxrregcount=N` (only when N>0). They go onto each optimizer's CUDA TUs
24	(`csrc/backends/cuda/sm_90/launch_<opt>.cu` and the megakernel cells
25	`csrc/fused/sm_90/mega_<model>_<opt>.cu`). The per-optimizer kernel header
26	`kernels/sm_90/<opt>_sm90.cuh` is `#include`d by `launch_<opt>.cu`, so flags on
27	the launcher TU reach the kernel body. Bindings (`*.cpp`), model-only TUs
28	(`models/<model>.cu`), and common/header TUs get **no** per-optimizer flags and
29	keep their in-header defaults. (`cluster_shape` and the feature macros — TMA /
30	WGMMA / fp8 / swizzle — are component-scoped and riskier; they are phase-2 and
31	are **not** emitted by this pass.)
32	
33	> If `_kernel_tuned.json` is absent the build is **byte-identical to before**:
34	> every kernel uses its `#ifndef SG_TUNED_*` default (block 256 / vec 4 /
35	> unroll 1 / async_depth 2; nvcc's own register allocator). A one-line notice
36	> is printed.
37	
38	---
39	
40	## 0. Prerequisites
41	
42	- A GPU host (the JIT autotuner builds + times real kernels). Steps 1 is
43	  GPU-bound; steps 2–4 only need a CUDA toolchain (`FORCE_CUDA=1` lets the
44	  build configure without a visible device).
45	- `ninja` on PATH (the injection hook patches torch's ninja writer; the build
46	  already requires `use_ninja=True`).

48	  exists): `FORCE_CUDA=1 pip install -e . --no-build-isolation`.

51	
52	## 1. Produce winners → `grokking_optimizers/_kernel_tuned.json`
53	
54	Run the JIT autotuner **once per optimizer** (optionally per model). Each run
55	read-merge-writes its winner into the canonical JSON, so 11 sequential runs
56	accumulate 11 entries under the arch key.
57	
58	```bash
59	# One optimizer (sm_90 / Hopper). Repeat for each of the 11.
60	python -m grokking_optimizers.compile \
61	    --optimizer adamw --model decoder --arch sm_90 \
62	    --cache build/.compile_cache.json \
63	    --jit-only --mode bayesian --bayesian-trials 300
64	```
65	
66	Optimizers: `adamw grokadamw grokfast lion looksam muon neuralgrok prodigy
67	supergrok11 supergrok15 supergrok2`. Models (short): `decoder vit mamba`.
68	
69	> **One winner per `(arch, optimizer)` — model is LAST-WINS.** The JSON schema
70	> is `{arch: {optimizer: {...}}}` (no model dimension), so tuning the same
71	> optimizer on a *second* model overwrites the first, and that single winner is
72	> applied to ALL of that optimizer's TUs — its `launch_<opt>.cu` AND every
73	> `mega_<model>_<opt>` megakernel cell across all models. If you tune `decoder`
74	> then `vit` for `adamw`, only `vit`'s `adamw` winner survives. Pick the model
75	> whose launch params you want shipped (the `"model"` field in each entry
76	> records which sweep produced it).
77	
78	A convenience loop:
79	
80	```bash
81	for opt in adamw grokadamw grokfast lion looksam muon \
82	           neuralgrok prodigy supergrok11 supergrok15 supergrok2; do
83	  python -m grokking_optimizers.compile \
84	      --optimizer "$opt" --model decoder --arch sm_90 \
85	      --cache build/.compile_cache.json --jit-only --mode bayesian
86	done
87	```
88	
89	> **Run optimizers SEQUENTIALLY, not in parallel processes.** The exporter's
90	> write is atomic (tmp + `os.replace`), so a reader never sees a half-written
91	> file — but it is read-merge-write, so two concurrent per-optimizer
92	> *processes* can clobber each other's just-written entry. One process at a
93	> time (the loop above) is safe. A failed JSON write is a loud warning in the
94	> compile report and **never** fails the tuning run; the winner is still in the
95	> compile cache and `tuned_configs.h`.
96	
97	Confirm the JSON was written and looks sane:
98	
99	```bash
100	python -c "import json;d=json.load(open('grokking_optimizers/_kernel_tuned.json'));\
101	import pprint;pprint.pprint({k:sorted(v) for k,v in d.items() if k!='_meta'});\
102	print('meta:',d.get('_meta'))"
103	```
104	
105	Schema (canonical, short arch key):
106	
107	```json
108	{
109	  "sm_90": {
110	    "adamw": {"block":256,"vec":4,"unroll":1,"async_depth":2,
111	              "maxrregcount":0,"model":"decoder"},
112	    "supergrok2": {"block":128,"vec":2,"unroll":4,"async_depth":3,

114	  },
115	  "_meta": {"timestamp":"…","source":"grokking_optimizers.compile.build_jit",
116	            "last_optimizer":"supergrok2","last_arch":"sm_90",
117	            "compile_py_version_hash":"…"}
118	}
119	```

1605	wiring**: one uniform scheduler/barrier substrate per arch, one parameterized

1607	single persistent launch, a Python code generator that instantiates that
1608	template per solver-chosen cell, and the `fused_step` dispatch that prefers a
1609	fused TU when present (§1.12). The Python feasibility solver
1610	(`grokking_optimizers/megakernel.py`) is the tier authority; the C++ generator
1611	mirrors its L3/L2/L1 model.

1613	### Scheduler / barrier design (§1.1–§1.4, §1.13, §1.14)
1614	
1615	Shared substrate — `csrc/fused/megakernel_common.cuh` (sm_90) and
1616	`csrc/fused/megakernel_common_hip.hip.hpp` (gfx942):
1617	
1618	- **§1.1 task-queue scheduler** — one global atomic `int` (`g_next_task`,
1619	  host-zeroed). Each persistent CTA/workgroup pulls parameter-tensor indices via
1620	  `atomicAdd(g_next_task, 1)` (the ThunderKittens-interpreter pattern). The
1621	  leader thread pulls per-CTA and broadcasts through shared/LDS (`next_block`).
1622	- **§1.2 work-stealing** — there is NO static partition: an idle core just keeps
1623	  calling `next()`, so a CTA that drains its tensor early grabs the next index.
1624	  The `atomicAdd` IS the steal.
1625	- **§1.3 SM/CU pinning** — `sm_id()` reads `%smid` (`mov.u32 %0, %%smid;`) on
1626	  sm_90; `cu_id()` reads `HW_ID` via `__builtin_amdgcn_s_getreg` on gfx942. The
1627	  host launches one persistent CTA per SM (gridDim.x = #SMs) / one workgroup per
1628	  CU, so that SM's/CU's optimizer-state slice stays L2-warm across the step.
1629	- **§1.4 hand-built grid barrier** — `GridBarrier` from two global atomics
1630	  (`arrived`, `generation`) + a **sense-reversing generation** counter, NO
1631	  cooperative launch (scales past the cooperative-grid CTA cap). Each CTA
1632	  samples the generation, RELEASE-fences its phase writes, joins the arrival
1633	  count; the **last arriver** resets `arrived=0` and advances the generation;
1634	  everyone else spins on the generation; all then ACQUIRE-fence. The
1635	  sense-reversal is what makes it **reusable** without the classic
1636	  reset-vs-lap race (a fast CTA cannot lap a slow one because the consumer side
